**


Students practice answering:

"What type of data do I have, and what database makes sense?"

For example:

Structured relational data

        ↓

       RDS

        ↓

Need higher-performance AWS relational database

        ↓

     Aurora

  

Massive key-value/document workload

        ↓

    DynamoDB

  

Data warehouse / analytics

        ↓

    Redshift

### Architecture Exercise

Build a simple application:

                   Users

                      |

                 Application

                    |

              ┌─────┴─────┐

              ↓           ↓

             S3          RDS

         Static files   Application

                        database

### End-of-Day Goal

Students can distinguish:

S3 vs EBS vs EFS

and

RDS vs DynamoDB vs Redshift

without relying on memorized definitions.

---

|   |   |   |
|---|---|---|
||RDS|DynamoDB|
|Type|Relational|NoSQL|
|Structure|Tables/relationships|Key-value/document|
|Query model|SQL|NoSQL APIs/query model|
|Scaling|Relational scaling patterns|Designed for massive scale|
|Best for|Structured relational workloads|High-scale key-value/document workloads|
